beats.narration: At the surface, the ocean seems to have no end.
beats.hero: The open ocean surface, horizon to horizon
beats.captions_shown: At the surface, the ocean seems to have no end.
beats.camera: 40 m above the sea on the trench axis, 34 km from Challenger Deep; slow forward drift toward the horizon; pitch eases from -8° to -30° (looking down at the water) by the end of the line.
beats.event: Low silver-blue sun, gentle swell; no other object in frame. The tilt down anticipates the dive.

beats.narration: But beneath the western Pacific, the seafloor drops into a world nearly eleven kilometres down.
beats.hero: The trench cut into the seabed, revealed as one immense cross-section
beats.captions_shown: But beneath the western Pacific, the seafloor drops into a world
beats.camera: Plunges through the surface just after 'beneath', pitching to look straight down; descends to ~2,500 m while travelling along the trench axis toward Challenger Deep, then raises its gaze down the trench.
beats.event: On 'seafloor' the seabed fades in below as a sonar-style relief; the trench opens beneath the camera by 'down'.

beats.narration: This is Challenger Deep, inside the Mariana Trench: the deepest known point in the ocean, measured at about ten thousand nine hundred thirty-five metres.
beats.hero: The deepest basin of the trench, ringed by one bathymetric contour

on_screen_text.replaces_caption: ten thousand nine hundred thirty-five metres.

beats.captions_shown: This is inside the Mariana Trench: the deepest known point in the ocean, measured at about
beats.camera: Glide down the trench axis from ~2,500 m to ~5,600 m (still above the hadal zone), looking ahead at the deepest basin.
beats.event: Depth contours glow on the trench relief; one ring is drawn around the deepest basin starting on 'Challenger'; the basin floor brightens slightly on 'ten'.

references.title: GEBCO 2019 and multibeam bathymetry of Challenger Deep and Sirena Deep
references.credit: Cassandra Bongiovanni, Heather A. Stewart and Alan J. Jamieson (Geoscience Data Journal, doi:10.1002/gdj3.122)

beats.narration: Sunlight vanishes far above it. Below six thousand metres lies the hadal zone:
beats.hero: A single narrow beam of sunlight, far above, fading to black

on_screen_text.replaces_caption: Below six thousand metres lies the hadal zone:

beats.camera: Tilts up toward the distant surface during the first sentence, then tilts back down and keeps descending into the trench.
beats.event: The beam dims to nothing by the end of 'above it'; on 'six thousand' the 6,000 m contour glows once along the trench walls and recedes as the camera passes below it.

beats.narration: near-freezing, pitch-dark, under pressure more than a thousand times the air at sea level.
beats.hero: The pressure gauge on a descending research lander

on_screen_text.replaces_caption: under pressure more than a thousand times the air at sea level.

beats.camera: Catches up with a descending lander in total darkness and slides past its gauge in a close three-quarter view.
beats.event: The sonar relief is gone: only the lander's lamps light the water. The gauge needle sweeps once to its high end on 'thousand'.

beats.narration: And still, life persists. Small animals inhabit these trenches, surviving in the darkness.
beats.hero: Pale hadal amphipods drifting into the lander's light
beats.captions_shown: And still, life persists. Small animals inhabit these trenches, surviving in the darkness.
beats.camera: Settles beside the lander's bait bag and slowly circles it.
beats.event: From 'life' onward, small pale amphipods swim in from the dark toward the bait. No bioluminescence; they are seen only where the lamp reaches.

beats.narration: The deepest fish ever filmed was found higher up, at eight thousand three hundred thirty-six metres, in another Pacific trench.
beats.hero: One snailfish gliding through the light

on_screen_text.replaces_caption: eight thousand three hundred thirty-six metres, in another Pacific trench.

beats.captions_shown: The deepest fish ever filmed was found higher up, at
beats.camera: Holds level while one translucent snailfish crosses the lamp light, then tilts down as the lander continues its descent.
beats.event: The fish enters on 'fish' and glides past in slow tail beats; it leaves the light before the line ends, staying well above the trench floor.

references.title: Pseudoliparis swirei, Mariana snailfish (Gerringer et al. 2017, Zootaxa 4358)
references.credit: Gerringer M.E., Linley T.D., Jamieson A.J., Goetze E., Drazen J.C. (2017)

beats.narration: At the bottom, our maps are still incomplete. Earth's deepest frontier is not another planet. It's beneath us.
beats.hero: The dark, vast floor of Challenger Deep
beats.captions_shown: At the bottom, our maps are still incomplete. Earth's deepest frontier is not another planet. It's beneath us.
beats.camera: Follows the lander down to the floor; after touchdown it slowly pulls back and rises, so the lander's pool of light becomes a small island in the dark. (Change from the draft plan's 'forward drift' — pending owner approval.)
beats.event: The floor emerges from black on 'bottom'; the lander settles in its own light; the darkness around it grows as the camera withdraws.

references.title: Challenger Deep floor with a stalked anemone, seen from DSV Limiting Factor (2022)
